resources.string: Models HR as a 1st-order dynamical system of Power: submaximal economy (HR@200W), response lag (\u03c4), and Fresh Model vs. Actual HR.

Heart Rate does not react instantaneously to pedaling power. It lags power fluctuations by a cardiorespiratory time constant (\u03c4 \u2248 30\u201345s). Static ratios (EF, Pw:Hr) misinterpret hilly terrain as cardiac fatigue. The 1st-order dynamical model extracts terrain-independent physiological parameters.
Your submaximal steady-state heart rate at a reference mechanical power of 200 Watts. Tracks seasonal aerobic fitness gains without all-out exhaustion tests (lower bpm = fitter).
How many extra heartbeats per minute the same power profile costs at the end of the ride compared to when fresh. Quantifies true cardiorespiratory fatigue, heat stress, and dehydration.
How fast your heart rate responds to acceleration and recovers on descents. Shorter \u03c4 indicates fresh, agile autonomic cardiac regulation; lengthening \u03c4 signals systemic fatigue.
How many additional Watts of mechanical work you produce per extra heartbeat. A steeper slope (more W/bpm) represents higher stroke volume and aerobic economy.
Fresh Model vs. Actual HR Graph

The Blue curve simulates what your heart rate would be throughout the ride if you remained as fresh as during the calibration window (minutes 8\u201355). The widening gap to your Actual HR (Red) visualizes progressive fatigue in real time.
